03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

The design system behind every page Swami publishes in his Vibe Coding style, and the skill that builds them. It turns a post, a video, a session, files, or notes into one browsable page whose look is locked: the same dark palette, fonts, and layout every time, so every page feels like part of one library.

Other skills hand their results to it: the web-conversation skills, the Fusion documentation skills, and the skill sheets (including this one) are all built on its template, patches, audio, and privacy rules. When this skill changes, all of them change with it.

Why it mattersDashboards built by hand drift: colors, fonts, and behaviors creep apart, and fixes made on one page never reach the next. Locking the design in one skill means every page gets the same features and every improvement reaches every new page.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • Locked lookBackground #0d0d0f, cyan accent #00e5ff, JetBrains Mono and DM Sans. Never new colors, fonts, or layouts; category accents come in order from one 8-color palette.
  • One fileEvery page is one self-contained .html file. Google Fonts is the only outside dependency, and images go in as data URIs.
  • Full widthHeader, table of contents, toolbar, sections, and footer all span the window; tables fit their width when opened and refit when it changes.
  • Kicker and summaryA short UPPERCASE kicker above the title, and section 01 is always the Dashboard Summary with a linked "What each section covers" table.
  • SearchSection 02 is always Search: words in any order, start of a word, small typos forgiven, "phrases" and -exclusions, filters, and a jump to every result.
  • Mind MapEvery page carries a Mind Map, built from the page itself, with zoom, pan, and hover cards on every bubble.
  • GlossaryTerms get a dotted underline that jumps to a Glossary with color-coded topics, and each term links back to every section that uses it.
  • Collapsed startEvery section and every item inside it starts collapsed; tables, callouts, and cards fold into labeled items listed in the table of contents.
  • TablesEvery table sorts, resizes, wraps words without breaking them, and keeps its header pinned under the section and item headers while you scroll.
  • Audio overviewA spoken overview (one female voice) sits under the title. Its narration follows Swami's pronunciation rules and a noun/verb stress check; if recording fails, a browser-voice player takes its place.
  • Privacy checkBefore every publish, people under NDA are kept off the page, its narration, and its data files.
  • House styleDays, dates, and times bold and bright; cyan ● bullets; topic IDs on list items; the Oxford comma; the footer "Vibe Coding: Swami · AI: Claude" with a mail link built at runtime; no © anywhere.
  • Publish as artifactPages are written in the working directory and published as private artifacts, with no runtime capabilities unless a feature needs one. This rule also overrides other skills' older save locations.
  • Version historyA nightly scheduled task backs up every published page to Swami's private GitHub repo, and script-built pages commit their sources too.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Any contentPosts, videos, chats, Zoom sessions, CAD or PLC files, links, and notes all become the same kind of page.
  • Same everywhereEvery page has the same look, controls, and features, so readers learn it once.
  • Large pagesIndex dashboards can search inside every dashboard they link to, with nightly refreshed data.
  • Owner-only partsRows, cards, or columns can be shown only to Swami, without any runtime capability.
  • Self-updating partsScript-built pages can be rebuilt by scheduled tasks, keeping their audio when the narration hasn't changed.
  • Recording needs networkThe first recording needs pip and GitHub downloads; on accounts that block them, the page falls back to the browser's own voice.
  • Owner-only isn't privateHidden parts still sit in the page source, so they are never used for anything under NDA.
  • Not a live viewA page shows what was true when it was built; it changes only when it is rebuilt or refreshed.
  • SizePages with audio run around 2 MB, most of it the embedded recording.
  • Dark onlyThe design is deliberately dark; there is no light version.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Patch orderRun the table-fit patch, then Search, then Mind Map, after the content sections are final; each is safe to re-run.
  • Double-escaped titlesA section title with & must be escaped once; escaping it twice breaks the table of contents and section links.
  • Bare # linksNever use href="#id" anchors; the artifact frame treats them as outside links. Navigation uses data-target and script.
  • Self-linksBody text that names a section becomes a link to it, so an intro starting "Search …" inside the Search section links to itself; reword it.
  • Zero-count termsA glossary term whose matcher hits nothing shows 0; reword the matcher or drop the term.
  • AcronymsNothing in an acronym's spelling says whether it is said as letters or as a word. Written in capitals the voice spells it out, so write letter acronyms in capitals (AI) and word acronyms as the word (cad, cam); ask Swami when unsure and add it to the Pronunciation table.
  • Stress checkThe voice often stresses two-syllable noun/verb words the wrong way ("REC-ords" for the verb); every narration gets the stress audit and phoneme markup.
  • Recording blockedIf pip or GitHub downloads are blocked, say why, use the browser-voice player, and point to Settings › Capabilities to allow GitHub's file servers.
  • Owner-only dataNever put anything under NDA in owner-only rows or columns: anyone with the link can read the page source.
  • Category colorsTwo categories with similar colors trigger a console warning; a finished page has none.
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • Code executionClaude's code execution must be on, with network access to the package registries and GitHub's file servers for the audio.
  • ArtifactsPublishing needs Claude's artifacts; pages start private.
  • Privacy listMemory names the people under NDA so every publish can check for them.
  • Owner buttonThe ↻ audio button needs the Claude Code Remote connector and the on-demand refresh task.

14Mind MapOVERVIEW▶

Everything on this page as one map, built from its sections, lists, tables, and callouts. HOVER OVER CONTROL FOR TOOLTIP. Click a bubble's › arrow to open or close its branch, and click a bubble's name to jump to that spot on the page. Hover any bubble for a short summary. The map opens fitted to its frame. Drag to pan; zoom with the − / + buttons, Ctrl/⌘ + scroll, or a pinch. Double-click empty space to fit the whole map again, Shift + click a bubble (or the space near one) to zoom to all the items in that branch, and drag a box with zoom region (or Alt/Option + drag) to zoom to just that area.

15GlossaryREFERENCE▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. Each term's Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section.
